questions: What are the costs associated with Operation 0, Operation 1, and Operation 2?
Can the same index in the sequence x be set to 1 multiple times, or is it only necessary to set it once?
Is it guaranteed that the input operations (L_i, R_i) will always cover all indices from 1 to N when combined, or must we verify this ourselves?
Are overlapping ranges between different operations allowed, and if so, how should they be handled?
If an index is already 1, does applying an operation that would set it to 1 again have any effect or cost?
Should the output format for the operations strictly follow the given format, or are variations acceptable?
In the case where N=0 or M=0, what should the expected behavior be?
Are there any hidden constraints or assumptions about the relationship between N and M that aren't explicitly stated?
answers: Operation 0 has cost 0; Operations 1 and 2 each have cost 1.
Once an index is set to 1, additional sets to 1 have no effect but still incur cost if from paid operations.
Not guaranteed; you must verify that the chosen operations cover all indices.
Overlapping ranges are allowed; the effect is simply that indices in the overlap are set to 1.
No additional effect, but the operation still incurs its cost if used in the solution.
Follow the exact specified output format.
Within the constraints, N and M are always positive; these edge cases are not expected.
No hidden constraints; only the explicitly stated constraints apply.
inline_prompts: There is an integer sequence x = (x_1, \ldots, x_N), which is initialized with x_1 = \cdots = x_N = 0. You will perform M operations on this integer sequence. In the i-th operation, you are given an integer pair (L_i, R_i) such that 1 \leq L_i \leq R_i \leq N, and you must perform exactly one of the following three operations: Operation 0 has cost 0; Operations 1 and 2 each have cost 1. This operation incurs a cost of. Operation 1: For each integer j with 1 \leq j \leq N, if L_i \leq j \leq R_i holds, set x_j = 1. This operation incurs a cost of. Operation 2: For each integer j with 1 \leq j \leq N, if L_i \leq j \leq R_i does not hold, set x_j = 1. This operation incurs a cost of. Your goal is to make x_1 = \cdots = x_N = 1 hold at the end. Determine whether this goal can be achieved. If it can be achieved, present one way to achieve it where the total cost of the operations is minimized. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N M L_1 R_1 \vdots L_M R_M Output If the goal is not achievable, print -1. If the goal is achievable, print one way to achieve it where the total cost of the operations is minimized, in the following format, where K is the minimum total cost of the operations, and \mathrm{op}_i is the type of operation (0, 1, or 2) chosen for the i-th operation. K \mathrm{op}_1 \cdots \mathrm{op}_M If there are multiple ways that minimize the total cost, printing any one of them is accepted. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 1000000 - 1 \leq M \leq 200000 - 1 \leq L_i \leq R_i \leq N - All input values are integers.
